Case A

A1. Searching the past seven days returned only the earlier requests from the one region. But the key was published at some point, and a scan can't show whether it was used before the burst. The search covers seven days, and we don't know how long ago publication was or whether the earlier requests were all legitimate. Within the search window, no misuse appears before the burst, and the earlier requests had a stable fingerprint. Still, "first misuse" depends on whether the 7-day window covers the period since publication. The burst came 19 minutes after publication, so the window almost certainly covers publication to burst, and the only requests in that span were the burst. Earlier requests, from before publication, are consistent with the legitimate owner. So the burst appears to be the first misuse, though it's not certain the burst was misuse. The question "was the burst the first misuse" suggests Yes, or at least no earlier misuse was seen. Cannot tell is tempting because the burst itself is not confirmed as misuse. But the burst has a different fingerprint, a residential proxy, and sensitive changes, so it is most likely misuse. I'll answer Yes.

A2. We don't know what evidence the check had available or what it used. Cannot tell.

A3. A shared destination is not enough to show one owner. No, not by itself.

A4. No reports after 30 days: no victim report or incident finding is recorded, but that is weak. The options are "Yes, weakly", "No", "Cannot tell". Absence of reports is weak evidence at best, and the payouts may have gone to an attacker-controlled destination with no victim to report. The destination is shared with two other accounts, which could be a mule destination. Absence of recorded reports doesn't indicate legitimacy, so I'll answer Cannot tell.

A5. Yes, it warrants investigation.

Case B

B1. D has 0 chargebacks against 2 for each of the others, with 100 transactions each. The recorded rate is lower (0% vs 2%). Yes.

B2. The combined measure is chargeback-or-alert at 5 percent. A combined figure doesn't show that no single account is above 5. No.

B3. The search found no accounts beyond A and the closed account, but it covered only what the search could match. It doesn't show there are none under other names. Cannot tell.

B4. The two notes are from different analysts, but they could have relied on the same evidence, and the notes are opinions. They are not independent confirmations. No.

B5. A blocked payment with no chargeback is not shown to be non-fraud, because it was blocked as suspected fraud. No.

B6. Yes, the shared templates and descriptor pattern justify investigating together.

RESULT CN-033 | A1: Yes | A2: Cannot tell | A3: No, not by itself | A4: Cannot tell | A5: Yes | B1: Yes | B2: No | B3: Cannot tell | B4: No | B5: No | B6: Yes
